column1: # Conformance vectors for the strict decoder.
# Line format: SCHEMA<TAB>HEX<TAB>EXPECTED, where EXPECTED is the full answer
# (ok<TAB>CONSUMED<TAB>REENCODED_HEX) or the bare category err / bad.  Expected `ok`
# lines were written by hand and cross-checked against borsh-rs where the schema
# has a Rust counterpart; they were not generated by the Lean code under test.
# Enum variants are listed in key order (ascending wire tag for the enums here).
# integers: little endian, fixed width, trailing bytes allowed (prefix decode)
# unit and the empty tuple encode to nothing
# floats: raw IEEE-754 bits, NaN (any payload, either sign) rejected, -0.0 distinct from 0.0
# string: u32 byte length then valid UTF-8 exactly as Rust core::str::from_utf8
# vec: u32 count then elements; a huge count with a short body must fail
# enums: u8 tag then the variant payload; unknown tags rejected; sparse (use_discriminant) tags
# maps: strictly ascending keys in the Rust Ord order (de_strict_order)
# signed integer keys order numerically, not by encoded bytes
# sets: same strictness as map keys
# zero-sized element/key types are ill-formed schemas (answered with bad)
# floats may not appear in map or set keys, at any depth
# schema text that does not parse or is not well-formed
# 128-bit boundary keys: signed order is -2^127 < -1 < 0 < 2^127-1, unsigned order is by value
